profiles.appearance: A dead-looking tree about 30 ft. tall, with thorny branches and trailing, rubbery roots.
notes: Grasping Root targets a creature the blight is not already grappling and deals no damage on impact. The creature is Grappled (escape DC 15) and takes 9 (1d6 + 6) bludgeoning at the start of each of its turns. A root has AC 15. One hit dealing at least 6 slashing severs it and ends the grapple without harming the blight.
Bite is a bonus action against a creature already Grappled by the blight.

profiles.name: Gazer
profiles.appearance: A tiny, floating sphere with one central eye, a toothy mouth and four smaller eyes on stalks.
notes: Eye Rays targets one or two creatures it sees within 60 ft. Roll twice on a d4 and reroll duplicates. Saves are DC 12.
1 · Dazing Ray. A failed Wisdom save leaves the creature Charmed until the start of the gazer’s next turn, halves its speed and gives it Disadvantage on attack rolls.
2 · Fear Ray. A failed Wisdom save leaves the creature Frightened until the start of the gazer’s next turn.
3 · Frost Ray. A failed Dexterity save deals 10 (3d6) cold damage.
4 · Telekinetic Ray. A Medium or smaller creature that fails a Strength save is moved up to 30 ft. away. The gazer can instead move a Tiny unattended object up to 30 ft. or manipulate it.

profiles.name: Kolyarut
profiles.appearance: An imposing metal construct with the appearance of an adjudicator.
notes: Multiattack uses Unerring Blade four times. Each blade automatically hits one target within 5 ft. for 24 force damage. Choose or roll its rider: 1–2 disarms one held item of the kolyarut’s choice, 3–4 removes reactions until the kolyarut’s next turn starts, and 5–6 pushes a Large or smaller target up to 15 ft. away.

Edict of Blades (Recharge 5–6). Move up to speed without provoking opportunity attacks and use Unerring Blade once against each creature passed. Each blade hit also ends spells of 5th level or lower on the target and Incapacitates it until the end of the kolyarut’s next turn.

Plane Shift (3/day). Cast with Intelligence and no material components. It may instead target one visible unwilling creature within 60 ft. A failed DC 18 Charisma save sends that creature to the Hall of Concordance in Sigil. Parry adds 6 AC against one attack that would hit while the kolyarut sees the attacker and wields a melee weapon.

profiles.name: Gazer
profiles.appearance: A tiny, floating sphere with one central eye, a toothy mouth and four smaller eyes on stalks.
notes: Eye Rays targets one or two creatures it sees within 60 ft. Roll twice on a d4 and reroll duplicates. Saves are DC 12.
1 · Dazing Ray. A failed Wisdom save leaves the creature Charmed until the start of the gazer’s next turn, halves its speed and gives it Disadvantage on attack rolls.
2 · Fear Ray. A failed Wisdom save leaves the creature Frightened until the start of the gazer’s next turn.
3 · Frost Ray. A failed Dexterity save deals 10 (3d6) cold damage.

4 · Telekinetic Ray. A Medium or smaller creature that fails a Strength save is moved up to 30 ft. away. The gazer can instead move an unattended object that weighs 10 lb. or less up to 30 ft. or manipulate it.

profiles.name: Aboleth
notes: Give the players a reason to leave dry ground. Put the captive or the only exit across the water and show what happened to someone who crossed first.

profiles.name: Animal Lord (Forager)
notes: Source variant of Animal Lord. Check the variant rules for changes to actions and traits.

profiles.name: Animal Lord (Hunter)
notes: Source variant of Animal Lord. Check the variant rules for changes to actions and traits.

profiles.name: Animal Lord (Sage)
notes: Source variant of Animal Lord. Check the variant rules for changes to actions and traits.

profiles.name: Beholder
notes: Break up sightlines with columns and a second elevation. Give players something they can move into the cone rather than leaving terrain as set dressing.

profiles.name: Cloaker
notes: Show loose fabric moving without a draft. Hang it near the back of the marching order so rescuing a grabbed character changes the party’s formation.

profiles.name: Death Tyrant
notes: Make retreat to a place beyond the cone possible. Put a fallen explorer just inside the area to show what recovery will cost.

profiles.name: Displacer Beast
notes: Let a burst of dust or dripping water hint at the gap between the creature and its image. Put cover along its route so the fight can move through the room.

profiles.name: Doppelganger
notes: Have the double know a recent public fact and miss an ordinary private habit. Give the players time to compare both people before a fight starts.

profiles.name: Empyrean (Fiend)
notes: Use Fiend as the creature type for this version.

profiles.name: Empyrean Iota (Fiend)
notes: Use Fiend as the creature type for this version.

profiles.name: Flumph
notes: Use it as a witness to a conversation the speakers thought was private. Its fear of being seen gives it a reason to ask the party for help.

profiles.name: Galeb Duhr
notes: Put a clear downhill channel through the encounter and give the party an uphill route. Let the group spot the stones marking the start of its run.
Rolling increases its walk speed to 30 feet, or to 60 feet downhill.

profiles.name: Gelatinous Cube
notes: Leave suspended keys or coins at chest height in a clean corridor. The clue gives cautious players a reason to stop before reaching the cube.

profiles.name: Mimic
notes: Place the mimic among several normal objects. Let it give itself away when a mundane clue, such as a drag mark or missing dust, fails to line up.

profiles.name: Otyugh
notes: Build the encounter around a passage through the refuse. The players can feed it, divert it, or risk letting it pull someone away from the group.

profiles.name: Owlbear
notes: Start with a blocked trail and the animal guarding food. Leave space to back away, lure it off the trail, or fight.

profiles.name: Roper
notes: Give the cave a side passage out of reach. Put discarded gear where the party can see it before entering the main chamber.

profiles.name: Rust Monster
notes: Give it a noisy scrap pile to follow. Players who notice what it is after can spend cheap metal to save better gear.

notes: Put safe lights on the far side of the marsh. Have the false guide lead the party toward a shortcut with a clear warning, such as submerged trail markers.

profiles.name: Black Bear
profiles.publication: Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2
profiles.appearance: Dark fur and a broad muzzle with rounded ears. The body is compact beside the brown bear.

Trait.name: Heightened Smell
Trait.effectNote: Use Perception 18 when relying on smell.

Action.name: Multiattack
Action.effectNote: Make one Bite and one Claws attack.

notes: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 13 and Stealth 10. Use Stealth instead of rolling when the creature hides.
Printed ability modifiers are STR +2, DEX +0, CON +2, INT -4, WIS +1, CHA -2.
Encounter habitat suggestions draw on the equivalent animal in Monster Manual (2024).
Kobold Press, Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2, p. 353.

profiles.name: Blood Hawk
profiles.publication: Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2
profiles.appearance: A russet-red hawk with a hooked bill and broad wings with pale undersides.

Trait.name: Heightened Sight
Trait.effectNote: Use Perception 19 when relying on sight.

Trait.name: Pack Tactics
Trait.effectNote: Attack rolls against a creature have advantage if a non-incapacitated ally is within 5 ft. of the target.

Bonus action.name: Evasive Flight
Bonus action.effectNote: While flying, take either the Disengage or Dodge action.

notes: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 14 and Stealth 12. Use Stealth instead of rolling when the creature hides.
Printed ability modifiers are STR -2, DEX +2, CON +0, INT -4, WIS +2, CHA -3.
Encounter habitat suggestions draw on the equivalent animal in Monster Manual (2024).
Kobold Press, Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2, p. 359.

profiles.name: Brown Bear
profiles.publication: Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2
profiles.appearance: Dense brown fur, a heavy shoulder hump and broad forepaws with long claws.

Trait.name: Heightened Smell
Trait.effectNote: Use Perception 18 when relying on smell.

Action.name: Multiattack
Action.effectNote: Make one Bite and one Claws attack. The bear grapples a creature hit by both attacks (escape DC 14). The bear can hold only one creature.

notes: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 13 and Stealth 10. Use Stealth instead of rolling when the creature hides.
Printed ability modifiers are STR +4, DEX +0, CON +3, INT -4, WIS +1, CHA -2.
Encounter habitat suggestions draw on the equivalent animal in Monster Manual (2024).
Kobold Press, Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2, p. 353.

profiles.name: Constrictor Snake
profiles.publication: Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2
profiles.appearance: A heavy brown snake with cream-edged blotches and thick muscular coils.

Action.name: Constrict
Action.effectNote: On a hit against a Large or smaller creature, grapple the target (escape DC 12). The target remains restrained and the snake cannot Constrict a different target until the grapple ends.

Bonus action.name: Crush
Bonus action.effectNote: One creature grappled by the snake makes a DC 12 STR save. On a failure, it takes 4 (1d8) bludgeoning damage and suffocates until the grapple ends.

notes: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 10 and Stealth 12. Use Stealth instead of rolling when the creature hides.
Printed ability modifiers are STR +2, DEX +2, CON +1, INT -5, WIS +0, CHA -4.
Encounter habitat suggestions draw on the equivalent animal in Monster Manual (2024).
Keensense perceives the surroundings within its listed radius without relying on sight.
The printed Crush line omits the word “save” after DC 12 STR. Resolve it as a Strength save.
Kobold Press, Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2, p. 369–370.

profiles.name: Dire Wolf
profiles.publication: Black Flag Roleplaying Reference Document v0.2

Companion use.name: Mounted combat
Companion use.effectNote: While used as a mount in mounted combat, it follows the controlled mount rules.

Source: Kobold Press, Player’s Guide 2 (2026), pp. 142–143.

profiles.name: Hound, Hunting
profiles.appearance: A small scent hound trained to track and flush quarry.

Trait.name: Diligent Tracker
Trait.effectNote: The hound has advantage on WIS (Survival) checks to track creatures.

Trait.name: Heightened Hearing and Smell
Trait.effectNote: Use Perception 18 when relying on hearing or smell.

Action.name: Bite
Action.effectNote: A hit grapples a Medium or smaller target (escape DC 12). While holding it, the hound cannot bite another target.

Bonus action.name: Flushing Bark
Bonus action.effectNote: In a 15-ft. cone, creatures that are hiding or behind cover make a DC 12 WIS save. Those that fail immediately stop hiding or move up to 10 ft. out of cover. This forced movement avoids opportunity attacks and damaging terrain.

Bonus action.name: Swift Hunter
Bonus action.effectNote: The hound moves up to its speed toward a hostile creature it can see.

Companion use.name: Cost and carrying capacity
Companion use.effectNote: 50 gp. It can carry 210 lb.

Companion use.name: Handler commands
Companion use.effectNote: A designated handler can use an action and pass a DC 10 WIS (Animal Handling) check to order it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide or Use an Object. On failure the animal defends itself and otherwise takes no action.

Companion use.name: Delivering or fetching an item
Companion use.effectNote: Use an Object can deliver an item. It can also fetch an item from a willing creature or one on the ground or otherwise unworn and uncarried.

Companion use.name: Mounted combat

notes: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 13 and Stealth 12. Ability modifiers are STR +1, DEX +2, CON +1, INT −4, WIS +1 and CHA −2. No languages or special senses.
The book prints CR 1/4. The publisher’s index rounds it to 0.3.
The handling rule specifies an Animal Handling check, then calls its failure a failed save. Resolve failure using the check it specifies.
Source: Kobold Press, Player’s Guide 2 (2026), pp. 142–144.

profiles.name: Oliphant Warbeast
profiles.appearance: A gray-brown pachyderm with four curved tusks, a short trunk and broad round ears.

Trait.name: Siege Monster
Trait.effectNote: It deals double damage to objects and structures.

Trait.name: Terrifying Siege
Trait.effectNote: Destroying a Small or larger object forces every hostile creature within 10 ft. to make a DC 16 CHA save. A failed save frightens the creature until the end of its next turn.

Trait.name: Trampling Charge
Trait.effectNote: After moving at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hitting it with Gore that turn, the target must pass a DC 16 STR save or fall prone. The warbeast can Stomp the target once as a bonus action if it is prone.

Trait.name: Condition resistance
Trait.effectNote: The block lists resistance to frightened, prone.

Action.name: Multiattack
Action.effectNote: Make one Gore and one Stomp attack or make two Gore attacks.

Action.name: Stomp
Action.effectNote: It can target only a prone creature.

Bonus action.name: Trunk Sweep
Bonus action.effectNote: Creatures in a 15-ft. cone make a DC 16 STR save or fall prone.

Companion use.name: Cost and carrying capacity
Companion use.effectNote: 2,400 gp. It can carry 1,560 lb.

Companion use.name: Handler commands
Companion use.effectNote: A designated handler can use an action and pass a DC 10 WIS (Animal Handling) check to order it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide or Use an Object. On failure the animal defends itself and otherwise takes no action.

Companion use.name: Delivering or fetching an item

The handling rule specifies an Animal Handling check, then calls its failure a failed save. Resolve failure using the check it specifies.
Source: Kobold Press, Player’s Guide 2 (2026), pp. 142–144.

profiles.name: Pig, War
profiles.appearance: A muscular pig with coarse brown-and-gray bristles and a pair of long curved tusks.

Trait.name: Charge
Trait.effectNote: Move at least 20 ft. straight toward the target and hit with Gore on the same turn. Add 5 (2d4) piercing damage. A creature hit this way must pass a DC 12 STR save or fall prone.

Trait.name: Heightened Smell
Trait.effectNote: Use Perception 16 when relying on smell.

Trait.name: Condition resistance
Trait.effectNote: The block lists resistance to grappled.

Bonus action.name: Frightful Squeal
Bonus action.effectNote: Every Beast and Humanoid within 10 ft. makes a DC 12 WIS save or becomes frightened until the end of its next turn.

Companion use.name: Cost and carrying capacity
Companion use.effectNote: 50 gp. It can carry 210 lb.

Companion use.name: Handler commands
Companion use.effectNote: A designated handler can use an action and pass a DC 10 WIS (Animal Handling) check to order it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide or Use an Object. On failure the animal defends itself and otherwise takes no action.

Companion use.name: Mounted combat
Companion use.effectNote: While used as a mount in mounted combat, it follows the controlled mount rules.

The handling rule specifies an Animal Handling check, then calls its failure a failed save. Resolve failure using the check it specifies.
Source: Kobold Press, Player’s Guide 2 (2026), pp. 142–145.

profiles.name: Pigeon, Homing
profiles.appearance: A small pigeon trained to carry messages in a tube fixed to its leg.

Trait.name: Messenger
Trait.effectNote: The pigeon knows the direction and approximate distance to up to three trained people or places on its plane. A humanoid can fasten a message tube and choose one of these destinations. The pigeon flies there directly and has resistance to exhaustion while carrying the tube.

Trait.name: Training
Trait.effectNote: It can learn up to three humanoids or places, with a week of training for each. Teaching a fourth replaces the destination it visited least recently. It uses these destinations in place of designated handlers.

Bonus action.name: Resolute Delivery
Bonus action.effectNote: It takes the Disengage or Dash action. Carrying a message tube also lets it move an extra 15 ft. before or after that action.

Companion use.name: Cost and carrying capacity
Companion use.effectNote: 8 gp. It can carry 15 lb.

notes: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 11 and Stealth 10. Ability modifiers are STR −4, DEX +0, CON +0, INT −4, WIS +1 and CHA −3. No languages or special senses.
The price table lists the 50-ft. flying speed. The stat block also gives a 10-ft. walking speed.
Source: Kobold Press, Player’s Guide 2 (2026), pp. 142–143.

profiles.name: Beetle, Giant Round
profiles.appearance: A Large, round-bodied beetle with a domed carapace, six legs and paired antennae.

Trait.name: Knockdown Charge
Trait.effectNote: Move at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature. The beetle can force it to make a DC 12 STR save or fall prone. If the target is prone, the beetle can Bite it once as a bonus action.

Reaction.name: Poison Spit
Reaction.effectNote: When the beetle takes damage, it can spit a 15-ft. line. Creatures in the line make a DC 12 DEX save. Failure deals 1d6 poison damage and leaves the creature poisoned for 1 minute. Success halves damage and prevents the condition. The creature can end the condition with a DC 12 CON save at the end of each of its turns.

Mount.name: Climbing and burrowing
Mount.effectNote: A rider has to pass a WIS (Animal Handling) check to stay on a climbing or burrowing mount. The DC starts at 10 and increases by 1 for every 5 ft. the mount moves that way.

Mount.name: Secure Saddle
Mount.effectNote: Fastening this saddle takes two rounds. It grants advantage on checks and saves to stay mounted.

notes: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 10 and Stealth 11. Ability modifiers are STR +3, DEX +1, CON +2, INT −5, WIS +0 and CHA −4. No languages.
The book calls it Round Beetle, Giant and prints CR 1/4. This profile uses the printed fraction for the existing Beetle, Giant Round entry, whose index value is 0.3.
Source: Kobold Press, Campaign Builder: Dungeons & Ruins (2025), pp. 28–29.

profiles.name: Earthworm, Giant
profiles.appearance: A Large earthworm with a long, legless, segmented body.

Trait.name: Water Aversion
Trait.effectNote: The worm refuses to enter bodies of water. If water fills its burrow while it is digging, it must Dash away from the water on its next turn.

Action.name: Thrash (Recharge 4–6)
Action.effectNote: Every creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 13 DEX save. Failure deals 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage and success halves it. A creature that fails by 5 or more also falls prone.

Reaction.name: Reflexive Writhe
Reaction.effectNote: If the worm can see a creature attacking it, it can raise its AC to 14 against that attack.

Mount.name: Climbing and burrowing
Mount.effectNote: A rider has to pass a WIS (Animal Handling) check to stay on a climbing or burrowing mount. The DC starts at 10 and increases by 1 for every 5 ft. the mount moves that way.

Mount.name: Secure Saddle
Mount.effectNote: Fastening this saddle takes two rounds. It grants advantage on checks and saves to stay mounted.

notes: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 10 and Stealth 11. Ability modifiers are STR +2, DEX +1, CON +3, INT −5, WIS +0 and CHA −4. No languages.
Source: Kobold Press, Campaign Builder: Dungeons & Ruins (2025), pp. 28–29.

profiles.name: Swarm of Skitterlings
profiles.appearance: A whirling flock of housecat-sized flying rodents, each with six clawed legs and a pair of leathery wings.

Trait.name: In Your Face
Trait.effectNote: An enemy sharing the swarm’s space makes attacks against other targets with disadvantage. It takes 3 (1d6) slashing damage if it attacks a creature besides the swarm.

Trait.name: Swarm
Trait.effectNote: The swarm and other creatures can share spaces. It fits through any opening that admits one Tiny skitterling. It cannot heal or gain temporary hit points.

Action.name: Claws
Action.effectNote: Reach 0 ft., one target. At 18 HP or fewer, the hit deals 7 (2d6) slashing damage. Any hit requires a DC 10 Constitution save. Failure blinds the target until the start of its next turn. Immunity to poison damage or the poisoned condition makes that save an automatic success.

notes: MCDM, Flee, Mortals! public preview, pp. 5 and 9. Unaligned. Proficiency bonus +2. No languages.
The Goblins chapter places outlaw goblin encounters in deserts, forests, and underground. The preview gives no separate natural habitat for this beast.
Goblins train skitterlings to attack faces. Put the swarm in an enemy’s space to pressure that enemy into attacking it, then use Claws to hinder the target’s next attacks.

profiles.name: War Spider
profiles.appearance: An enormous eight-legged spider with blade-edged legs and a broad back that can carry a goblin archery platform.

Trait.name: Baby Burst
Trait.effectNote: At death, release one Swarm of Insects (spiders). It acts on the War Spider’s initiative count.

Trait.name: Rider Launcher
Trait.effectNote: An allied rider jumping off the spider can long jump 30 ft. or high jump 15 ft. from a standstill or running start. The rider has advantage on its first melee weapon attack that turn.

Trait.name: Spider Climb
Trait.effectNote: The spider can climb difficult surfaces and traverse ceilings without a check.

Trait.name: Web Walker
Trait.effectNote: Webbing does not restrict the spider’s movement.

Trait.name: Wide Back
Trait.effectNote: Two Small or Tiny riders can share a space on the spider. It carries up to 18 Small or 64 Tiny riders.

Action.name: Web Spray
Action.effectNote: Each creature in a 15-ft. cube must make a DC 13 Dexterity save or be restrained. A creature can use an action to attempt a DC 13 Strength or Dexterity check, freeing itself or a creature within its reach on a success.

Action.name: Trample (Recharge 6)
Action.effectNote: Move up to its speed through other creatures’ spaces. Make one Bladed Leg attack against each creature whose space the spider enters. A hit removes that creature’s reactions until the start of its next turn.

notes: MCDM, Flee, Mortals! public preview, pp. 5 and 9. Unaligned. Proficiency bonus +2. No languages.
The Goblins chapter places outlaw goblin encounters in deserts, forests, and underground. The preview gives no separate natural habitat for this beast.
Goblins use the spider as a battle mount, with archers above and riders that jump into melee. Use Web Spray to hold a group in place or Trample to move through an enemy line.

profiles.name: Ambush Vine
profiles.appearance: A mass of long, thorny vines that can blend into surrounding vegetation.

powers.name: Lashing Vines
powers.damage: 2d8 + 6, with additional effects against immobilized enemies

Power details.name: Poison Lash
Power details.effectNote: Melee basic attack, reach 2 squares. Poison keyword.

Power details.name: Foot Snare
Power details.effectNote: Reach 4 squares. A hit knocks the target prone.

Power details.name: Lashing Vines
Power details.effectNote: Healing keyword. Close burst 4 against enemies. Each hit on an immobilized target deals an extra 1d8 damage and restores 5 HP to the vine.

Power details.name: Rapid Growth
Power details.effectNote: Encounter power. When first bloodied, the vine spawns two Ambush Vine Shoots within 4 squares. They act immediately after the vine on its initiative count.

Power details.name: Sprout Vine
Power details.effectNote: At-will minor action. The vine takes 10 damage and spawns one Ambush Vine Shoot within 4 squares. The shoot acts immediately after the vine on its initiative count.

Ambush Vine Shoot.name: Level 15 Minion Controller
Ambush Vine Shoot.effectNote: Medium fey beast (plant), 300 XP. Initiative +14, Perception +14, tremorsense 20, AC 29, Fortitude 27, Reflex 30, Will 23. Speed 6 squares and burrow 6. It has 1 HP and takes no damage from a missed attack.

Ambush Vine Shoot.name: Wrapping Vines
Ambush Vine Shoot.effectNote: Standard at-will melee basic attack, reach 2 squares. +20 vs. Fortitude. Hit for 12 damage and restrain the target (save ends).

Ambush Vine Shoot.name: Enwrap
Ambush Vine Shoot.effectNote: Enemies adjacent to the shoot take a −2 penalty to saving throws against immobilized and restrained.

Ambush Vine Shoot.name: Ability scores and Stealth
Ambush Vine Shoot.effectNote: Str 18, Dex 25, Con 16, Int 2, Wis 15, Cha 12. Stealth +19, or +24 in undergrowth, trees, or swamps. Unaligned. No languages.

notes: August 2012 update, p. 82, corrects the parent vine’s original 1,400 XP to 2,800 XP. The shoot’s 300 XP comes from its own block.
Unaligned. No languages. Saving throws +2 and one action point. Stealth rises from +20 to +25 in undergrowth, trees or swamp.
The vine stalks prey through canopy, soil and water. It can hide underground or blend with surrounding plants.
Source: Wizards of the Coast, Monster Manual 2 (4e), pp. 204–205, with the August 2012 Rules Update, p. 82.

profiles.name: Pseudodragon
profiles.appearance: A small winged drake with a fanged muzzle, clawed feet, and a stinging tail.

Power details.name: Sting
Power details.effectNote: Melee basic attack with the Poison keyword.

Power details.name: Flyby Attack
Power details.effectNote: At-will standard action. Fly up to 8 squares and make one melee basic attack along that route. Moving away from that target does not provoke its opportunity attacks.

Power details.name: Invisibility
Power details.effectNote: Standard action with the Illusion keyword. It recharges when the pseudodragon takes damage. Invisibility lasts while the pseudodragon stays still.

notes: August 2012 update, p. 77, changes the original size from Tiny to Small. The checked Deluxe page already shows Small.
Unaligned. No languages. It communicates with animal noises. Wild pseudodragons hunt other creatures and usually leave humanoids alone unless provoked. Some live with humanoids as pets.
The tactics use Sting during a Flyby Attack when it is available. Against a persistent enemy the pseudodragon shifts, then uses Invisibility.
Source: Wizards of the Coast, Monster Manual (4e Deluxe), pp. 90–92, with the August 2012 Rules Update, p. 77.

profiles.name: Giant Fly
profiles.appearance: A rideable giant horsefly brought to life from the Ebony Fly figurine.

Figurine.name: Activation
Figurine.effectNote: Use an action to speak the command word and throw the figurine to a point on the ground within 60 ft. The fly appears if the space is free and large enough.

Figurine.name: Mount and commands
Figurine.effectNote: The fly is friendly, understands the activator’s languages through the item, and follows spoken commands. Without orders it limits itself to self-defense. It can carry a rider for up to 12 hours.

Figurine.name: Reversion and reuse
Figurine.effectNote: The fly becomes a figurine again at the end of 12 hours, at 0 HP, or if the activator uses an action to repeat the command word while touching it. Wait two days before using it again.

notes: Unaligned. The stat block lists no languages. The figurine rules give the fly its understanding of spoken commands.
The 5.1 block supplies no actions, challenge rating, XP, proficiency bonus, or initiative value. The 5.2.1 version supplies CR 0 and is a separate printing.
Source: Wizards of the Coast, System Reference Document 5.1, pp. 221–222.

profiles.name: Bat
profiles.appearance: A small insect-eating bat with short fur and thin membranes stretched between its elongated wing fingers.

combat.attackOptions: Space 1 ft. and reach 0 ft. No attack or full attack is listed.

notes: Always neutral. Organization as printed: Colony (10–40) or crowd (10–50).
Feats: Alertness.
Small nocturnal insect-eater. The SRD supplies no natural attack.

Trait.name: Blindsense (Ex)
Trait.effectNote: Within 20 ft. and with line of effect the bat can locate creatures without relying on sight. A creature it cannot see still has total concealment. The bat loses the +4 racial bonus included in both Listen and Spot when it loses blindsense.

profiles.name: Cat
profiles.appearance: A housecat with striped fur, a flexible body, a long tail and retractile claws.

combat.attackOptions: Space 2-1/2 ft. and reach 0 ft. Attack: Claw +4 melee (1d2–4). Full attack: 2 claws +4 melee (1d2–4) and bite –1 melee (1d3–4).

notes: Always neutral. Organization as printed: Domesticated or solitary.
Feats: Weapon Finesse.
The common housecat stalks prey. Its 0 ft. reach requires entering the target’s space for melee attacks.

Monster Manual errata grants Stealthy and makes Weapon Finesse a bonus feat. It raises Hide to +16, or +20 in tall grass or heavy undergrowth, and Move Silently to +8. Use the original SRD values for this printing.
A hit whose printed damage roll falls below 1 deals a minimum of 1 damage before defenses.

Trait.name: Scent (Ex)
Trait.effectNote: Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., 60 ft. if upwind or 15 ft. if downwind. Use a move action to find the direction. Pinpoint the creature within 5 ft.

Trait.name: Cat skills
Trait.effectNote: Includes +4 racial to Climb, Hide and Move Silently, and +8 racial to Balance and Jump. Use Dexterity for Climb and Jump. Hide increases from +14 to +18 in tall grass or heavy undergrowth.

profiles.name: Dog
profiles.appearance: A small dog weighing about 20 to 50 pounds, with a narrow muzzle, four padded paws and a mobile tail.

combat.attackOptions: Space 5 ft. and reach 5 ft. Attack and full attack each use one Bite attack.

notes: Always neutral. Organization as printed: Solitary or pack (5–12).
Feats: Alertness, Track as a bonus feat.
The SRD prints CR 1/3. The catalog previously had a blank CR. Dogs may chase prey in packs.

Trait.name: Scent (Ex)
Trait.effectNote: Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., 60 ft. if upwind or 15 ft. if downwind. Use a move action to find the direction. Pinpoint the creature within 5 ft.

Trait.name: Tracking
Trait.effectNote: The dog has Track as a bonus feat. Its +4 racial bonus when tracking by scent raises Survival from +1 to +5. Its Jump score includes +4 racial.

profiles.name: Giant Constrictor Snake
profiles.appearance: An enormous, thick-bodied snake with overlapping scales. Its muscular coils are broad enough to wrap around large prey.

combat.attackOptions: Space 15 ft. and reach 10 ft. Attack and full attack each use one Bite attack.

notes: Always neutral. Organization as printed: Solitary.
Feats: Alertness, Endurance, Skill Focus (Hide), Toughness.

Endurance grants +4 on endurance and exposure checks and saves, including Swim to resist nonlethal damage and Constitution checks for continuing to run, forced marches, holding breath, and avoiding starvation or thirst.
Advancement: 12–16 HD (Huge); 17–33 HD (Gargantuan).
The giant entry gives the damage and uses the constrictor family rules to resolve the hold.

Special attack.name: Improved Grab (Ex)
Special attack.effectNote: After hitting with Bite, start a grapple as a free action against a smaller target without provoking an attack of opportunity. Win the grapple check to pull the target into the snake’s space. It can hold using only its mouth at a −20 grapple penalty and avoid taking the grappled penalties.

Special attack.name: Constrict (Ex)
Special attack.effectNote: A successful grapple check deals 1d8+10 constriction damage. Apply the normal improved-grab weapon damage on later successful grapple checks to maintain the hold as well.

Trait.name: Scent (Ex)
Trait.effectNote: Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., 60 ft. if upwind or 15 ft. if downwind. Use a move action to find the direction. Pinpoint the creature within 5 ft.

Trait.name: Snake skills
Trait.effectNote: The listed modifiers include +4 racial to Hide, Listen and Spot, and +8 racial to Balance and Climb. Use the higher of Strength or Dexterity for Climb. The snake can take 10 on Climb even when rushed or threatened.

Trait.name: Swim
Trait.effectNote: The listed modifier includes the +8 racial bonus for hazards or special maneuvers. Take 10 even when threatened or distracted. It can run while swimming in a straight line.

profiles.name: Heavy Horse
profiles.appearance: A large working horse with a broad chest, powerful shoulders and a heavy build like a Clydesdale.

combat.attackOptions: Space 10 ft. and reach 5 ft. Attack: Hoof –1 melee (1d6+1). Full attack: 2 hooves –1 melee (1d6+1).

notes: Always neutral. Organization as printed: Domesticated.
Feats: Endurance, Run.

Endurance grants +4 on endurance and exposure checks and saves, including Swim to resist nonlethal damage and Constitution checks for continuing to run, forced marches, holding breath, and avoiding starvation or thirst.

Trait.name: Scent (Ex)
Trait.effectNote: Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., 60 ft. if upwind or 15 ft. if downwind. Use a move action to find the direction. Pinpoint the creature within 5 ft.

Trait.name: Carrying capacity
Trait.effectNote: Light up to 200 lb., medium 201–400 lb., heavy 401–600 lb. Can drag 3,000 lb.

Trait.name: Mounted combat
Trait.effectNote: The horse cannot fight while carrying a rider. It rarely attacks with its hooves. The listed secondary hoof attack adds half its Strength modifier to damage. A rider controlling it in battle makes a DC 20 Ride check as a move action.

Trait.name: Run
Trait.effectNote: Run at five times speed with up to medium armor and load, or four times with heavy armor or load. Add +4 to Jump with a running start. Keep the Dexterity bonus to AC.

profiles.name: Heavy Warhorse
profiles.appearance: A broad-chested warhorse bred for strength, with a heavy neck and powerful hindquarters.

combat.attackOptions: Space 10 ft. and reach 5 ft. Attack: Hoof +6 melee (1d6+4). Full attack: 2 hooves +6 melee (1d6+4) and bite +1 melee (1d4+2).

notes: Always neutral. Organization as printed: Domesticated.
Feats: Endurance, Run.

Endurance grants +4 on endurance and exposure checks and saves, including Swim to resist nonlethal damage and Constitution checks for continuing to run, forced marches, holding breath, and avoiding starvation or thirst.

Trait.name: Scent (Ex)
Trait.effectNote: Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., 60 ft. if upwind or 15 ft. if downwind. Use a move action to find the direction. Pinpoint the creature within 5 ft.

Trait.name: Carrying capacity
Trait.effectNote: Light up to 300 lb., medium 301–600 lb., heavy 601–900 lb. Can drag 4,500 lb.

Trait.name: Mounted combat
Trait.effectNote: The warhorse can attack while ridden. A DC 10 Ride check as a free action lets the rider and mount both attack.

Trait.name: Run
Trait.effectNote: Run at five times speed with up to medium armor and load, or four times with heavy armor or load. Add +4 to Jump with a running start. Keep the Dexterity bonus to AC.

profiles.name: Huge Viper Snake
profiles.appearance: An enormous viper with broad coils, a distinct head and hinged venomous fangs.

combat.attackOptions: Space 15 ft. and reach 10 ft. Attack and full attack each use one Bite attack.

notes: Always neutral. Organization as printed: Solitary.
Feats: Improved Initiative, Run, Weapon Focus (bite).
Advancement: 7–18 HD (Huge).
The RTF, and linked HTML print flat-footed AC 15. Subtracting its +2 Dexterity from AC 15 gives 13. Use the printed 15 for this record.

Special attack.name: Poison (Ex)
Special attack.effectNote: After a damaging bite, save immediately and again 1 minute later even if the first save succeeds. Each failure deals 1d6 Constitution damage. The viper is immune to its own venom and that of others of its kind.

Trait.name: Scent (Ex)
Trait.effectNote: Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., 60 ft. if upwind or 15 ft. if downwind. Use a move action to find the direction. Pinpoint the creature within 5 ft.

Trait.name: Snake skills
Trait.effectNote: The listed modifiers include +4 racial to Hide, Listen and Spot, and +8 racial to Balance and Climb. Use the higher of Strength or Dexterity for Climb. The snake can take 10 on Climb even when rushed or threatened.

Trait.name: Swim
Trait.effectNote: The listed modifier includes the +8 racial bonus for hazards or special maneuvers. Take 10 even when threatened or distracted. It can run while swimming in a straight line.

profiles.name: Large Shark
profiles.appearance: A heavy-bodied shark about 15 feet long, with a triangular dorsal fin and powerful jaws.

combat.attackOptions: Space 10 ft. and reach 5 ft. Attack and full attack each use one Bite attack.

notes: Always neutral. Organization as printed: Solitary, school (2–5), or pack (6–11).
Feats: Alertness, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative.
Advancement: 8–9 HD (Large).

Trait.name: Blindsense (Ex)
Trait.effectNote: While underwater, locate underwater creatures within 30 ft. and line of effect. Unseen creatures still have total concealment.

Trait.name: Keen Scent (Ex)
Trait.effectNote: Detect creatures by scent within 180 ft. and blood in water up to 1 mile away.

traits: Ratlike humanoid with a long muzzle, prominent incisors, rough fur, and a mostly bare tail. The printed setting describes Nezumi in Rokugan and the Shadowlands.
Medium. Base land speed 40 ft. Constitution +2, Charisma −2.
Low-light vision extends useful vision to twice the human distance in dim conditions while retaining color and detail.
Racial +2 to Hide and Move Silently. Racial +2 on saves against poison and disease.
Immune to acquiring a Shadowlands Taint score and to ill effects of direct Shadowlands exposure. Cloud of Taint and special attacks from Shadowlands creatures can still harm a Nezumi.
Claw or bite deals 1d4 normal damage as an unarmed strike. Choose one of these unarmed attacks per round.
Keen Scent permits the optional Scent feat at Wisdom 11 or higher. It does not grant that feat automatically.

With Scent, detect a presence as a free action within 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind, or 15 ft. downwind. Strong odors double these ranges and overpowering odors triple them. Finding direction costs a move-equivalent action. Pinpoint within 5 ft.

With Scent, follow a trail using Wisdom. A fresh trail is usually DC 10 and the DC rises by 2 per hour. Scent and group size can modify it. Surface and visibility penalties do not apply. A Nezumi can recognize familiar odors. Water can erase a trail. Strong masking odors hamper detection and identification and raise the base tracking DC to 20. Other tracking rules follow the Track feat.
Automatic languages Rokugani and Nezumi. Bonus languages Bakemono and Shadowlands. Favored class Rogue.

species.name: Hengeyokai
traits: A playable shapechanger with three forms: human, animal, and bipedal hybrid. Choose one animal kind. A character keeps that animal kind and its corresponding hybrid throughout play.

Alternate Form is supernatural. Each transition uses one of 1 + actual character level uses per day. It takes a full-round action and provokes attacks of opportunity. It follows the D&D 3.0 Polymorph Other spell with the exceptions below.

Animal and hybrid forms have low-light vision and can communicate with their own animal kind. The 2003 FAQ confirms Medium hybrids. Apply the hybrid adjustment to current physical scores.
Gear stays intact between human and hybrid forms and reappears after leaving animal form. A hybrid typically uses light or medium armor. Heavy armor is unavailable in hybrid form.
Automatic languages Common and Hengeyokai. Bonus languages Giant, Goblin, Nezumi, and Spirit Tongue. Favored class Wu jen.
Level adjustment affects experience and starting equipment. A first-level Hengeyokai has ECL 2 but still has two form changes per day.

species.name: Dromite
traits: A Small Monstrous Humanoid with the Psionic subtype. Charisma +2, Strength −2, Wisdom −2. Base land speed 20 ft. and darkvision 60 ft. Humanoid-only effects such as charm person do not apply.
Small size gives +1 to AC and attack rolls, +4 to Hide, −4 to grapple, smaller weapons, and three-quarters of a Medium creature’s carrying capacity.
Chitin grants +3 natural armor and energy resistance 5. Choose a caste at character creation. The resistance stacks with energy resistance from other effects.
Naturally Psionic grants 1 bonus power point at 1st level. Manifesting powers requires a separate source, such as a psionic class.

Racial Energy Ray is a psi-like ability usable once per day. It matches the caste’s energy resistance. Manifester level equals half the character’s Hit Dice, rounded down, minimum 1. It costs no power points and automatically augments to that manifester level.

Energy Ray takes a standard action and uses a ranged touch attack. Range is 25 ft. plus 5 ft. per two manifester levels. It allows no saving throw. Power resistance applies. Roll one d6 per manifester level before the caste’s damage adjustment.

Scent reaches 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind, or 15 ft. downwind. Strong odors double that distance and overpowering odors triple it. A move action identifies direction. Within 5 ft., scent pinpoints the source.
Blind-Fight is a bonus feat. Compound eyes give +2 racial bonus on Spot checks. Automatic language Common. Bonus languages Dwarven, Gnome, Goblin, Terran.
Favored class Wilder. Level adjustment +1. A first-level Dromite has ECL 2.
Fire Caste has fire resistance 5. Add +1 damage per die. At manifester level 1, the ray deals 1d6+1 fire damage.

traits: Medium Aberration with the Psionic subtype. Charisma −2, land speed 30 ft., and no darkvision. Humanoid-only effects such as charm person do not apply.

Naturally Psionic grants 2 bonus power points at 1st level. Manifesting powers requires a separate source, such as a psionic class. The 2006 errata confirms 2 points for the creature chapter’s Elan as well.
Resistance (Su). Spend 1 power point as an immediate action for a +4 racial bonus on all saving throws until the beginning of your next action.
Resilience (Su). Spend power points as an immediate action when about to take damage. Reduce the incoming damage by 2 HP per power point spent.
Repletion (Su). Spend 1 power point to go without food or water for 24 hours. Use the core standard-action default for supernatural abilities.
An immediate action uses your swift action on your turn or on the following turn if used outside your turn. You cannot take one while flat-footed.

A four-hour daily trance provides the benefit of eight hours of human sleep. The 2006 errata removes maximum age. The aging thresholds remain 200 years for middle age, 400 for old, and 1,000 for venerable.
Elans emerge from a psionic ritual undergone by adult humans. A new Elan retains basic memories and personality and starts again as a 1st-level character with new classes and skills.
Automatic language Common. Bonus languages may include any nonsecret language. Favored class Psion. Level adjustment +0.

species.name: Raptoran
traits: Medium Humanoid with the Raptoran subtype. Base land speed 30 ft. The playable entry gives no racial ability-score adjustment or level adjustment.
Wing-Aided Movement gives +10 racial bonus to Jump checks. +2 racial bonus to Climb and Spot. Low-light vision reaches twice human distance in dim light and retains color and detail.

Gliding (Ex) uses 40-ft. speed and average maneuverability. Descend 5 ft. per 20 ft. traveled forward. Gliding prevents falling damage and never allows hovering. A medium or heavy load prevents gliding.
If unconscious or helpless in midair, the wings stiffen and unfold. The Raptoran descends in a corkscrew and takes only 1d6 falling damage regardless of distance.
At 5 Hit Dice, Flight (Ex) grants a 40-ft. fly speed with average maneuverability. A medium or heavy load, fatigue, or exhaustion prevents powered flight.

At 5–9 Hit Dice, fly safely for a number of consecutive rounds equal to your Constitution modifier, minimum 1. You can fly for up to twice that many rounds, becoming fatigued at the end of the flight. You also become fatigued after more than 10 minutes total powered flight in a day. Glide before, after, or between rounds of powered flight.

At 10 Hit Dice, keep the 40-ft. average fly speed and fly with no more exertion than walking or running. The playable text leaves the daily cutoff implicit, while several 10+ HD sample NPCs still list fatigue after 10 minutes.

Once powered flight is available at 5 Hit Dice, it permits a straight-line run and a diving charge with a piercing weapon. The dive must move at least 30 ft. and descend at least 10 ft. A hit deals double damage.
Pact with Wind Lords gives +1 caster level when casting air-descriptor spells. Unerring Direction senses north even underground on the Material Plane.

A footbow is a martial weapon for a Raptoran, with a 110-ft. range increment. Grip it with the feet and draw with one hand for the usual Strength bonus, or draw with both hands to apply 1½ times the bonus. The bow’s Strength rating caps the bonus before the multiplier. On the ground, fire from a prone position at −4 to the attack roll.
Common and Tuilvilanuue are automatic. Bonus languages Draconic, Elven, Gnome, Goblin, Orc, Sylvan. Favored class Cleric.

traits: Medium Humanoid with the Human subtype. Base land speed 30 ft. The entry lists no ability adjustments, racial Hit Dice, or level adjustment.
Luminous Sigils (Su) orbit the head and give candlelight. Douse them as a standard action to suspend power sigil bonuses and word abilities. Restore them as a free action.
Sigils are insubstantial and disappear into matter they touch. A change of form keeps the sigils if the new form preserves the Illumian’s supernatural abilities.

Glyphic Resonance (Ex) applies when a spell’s name includes glyph, rune, sigil, or symbol. If the Illumian’s character level is below the spell’s caster level, take a −4 racial penalty on its saves. At or above that caster level, gain immunity to the spell.

Power Sigils (Su) grant one choice at 1st level for a +1 bonus. Page 54 gives a second distinct sigil at 2nd level in any class, raising both bonuses to +2. On p. 87, Bloodwing Zhaolei is a Bard 1/Fighter 1 with two +2 sigils and the Vaulaesh word. Spot DC 10 distinguishes a power sigil and Knowledge (arcana) DC 15 identifies it.

Aesh adds to Strength checks and Strength-based skill checks. Hoon adds to Constitution and Wisdom checks and skills based on either ability. Naen adds to Intelligence checks and Intelligence-based skill checks.

Uur adds to Dexterity checks and Dexterity-based skill checks. Vaul adds to Charisma checks and Charisma-based skill checks. Krau adds to caster level for spells and spell-like abilities, capped at character level.
Illumian Words (Su) come from combining two power sigils. When a word calls for an unprepared spell slot, a slot that holds a prepared spell is ineligible.
Aeshkrau and Uurkrau allow Strength and Dexterity respectively to determine bonus spells for a high ability score in any or all of the Illumian’s spellcasting classes.
Aeshoon spends a turn or rebuke attempt as a swift action, twice per day, to add the Wisdom bonus to damage with Weapon Focus weapons until the next turn begins.
Aeshuur grants a +2 dodge bonus to AC against a target damaged by the Illumian’s sneak attack or critical hit, until the Illumian’s next turn begins.

Hoonkrau uses a swift action and a turn attempt to add 1d8 healing to cure spells, or a rebuke attempt to add 1d8 damage to inflict spells. The effect lasts through the end of the next turn. Use twice per day.
Hoonvaul spends a spell slot as a swift action, twice per day, to add its level to turning checks and turning damage and to a smite attack’s attack and damage rolls until the next turn begins.
Naenaesh can leave up to two slots empty during preparation. Until the next preparation, those slots stay empty and other spells prepared at their levels can be cast with Still Spell.

Naenhoon uses a swift action, twice per day, to apply a metamagic feat the Illumian has. Spend turn or rebuke attempts equal to the feat’s level adjustment. Casting time, spell slot, and effective spell level stay the same. Heighten Spell changes the effective level and costs one turn attempt per level added, up to spell level 9.

Naenkrau can leave up to two slots empty during preparation, at different levels if choosing two. Other spells of those levels gain +1 to their save DC, including spells from other classes. The slots stay empty and the bonus lasts until next preparation.

Uurhoon spends a slot as a swift action, twice per day. For one minute per slot level, apply the Wisdom bonus as an insight bonus to Reflex saves and the Dexterity bonus as an insight bonus to caster level checks against spell resistance.

Uurnaen can leave one 1st- or 2nd-level slot empty during preparation. Until next preparation, the slot stays empty and its level gives an insight bonus on attack rolls for unarmed strikes and sneak attacks.
Vaulaesh spends a slot as a swift action, twice per day. Its level is an insight bonus to AC and to Weapon Focus weapon damage until the Illumian’s next turn begins.
Vaulkrau spends a slot as an immediate action, twice per day. Its level is an insight bonus on the next save made before the Illumian’s next turn begins.
Vaulnaen uses an available slot twice per day to cast any prepared spell of the same level spontaneously, at the caster level of the class that prepared it.
Vauluur spends a slot as a swift action, twice per day, to add 1d6 per slot level to unarmed strike damage and sneak attack damage until the Illumian’s next turn begins.
Final Utterance (Ex) releases audible Illumian syllables at death for 1 round per Hit Die, even if the body is destroyed. Anyone within earshot can hear it.
+2 racial bonus on saves against spells with the shadow descriptor.
Superior Literacy means every Illumian is literate and Speak Language is always a class skill. Common and Illumian are automatic. Any nonsecret language may be taken as a bonus language.
Favored class Any. Exclude the highest class when figuring multiclass XP penalties. An Illumian monk or paladin can return to that class after multiclassing.

traits: Medium Outsider with the Earth subtype. The printed profile lists Extraplanar. Apply that subtype when away from the native plane. Base land speed 30 ft. Darkvision sees in black and white out to 60 ft.
Full ancestry gives +8 Strength, +8 Constitution, +2 Intelligence, −2 Charisma, and +4 natural armor.
Immune to acid and poison.

Full ancestry has 2d8 racial Hit Dice, BAB +2, and base Fortitude, Reflex, and Will +3 each. It grants one feat plus Blind-Fight as a bonus feat. Level adjustment +4 gives ECL 6 before any class levels.

Racial skill points are 5 × (8 + Intelligence modifier). Racial class skills are Appraise, Climb, Craft (stoneworking), Intimidate, Knowledge (history), Knowledge (the planes), Listen, Search, Spot, and Survival.
Proficient with simple and martial weapons, light and medium armor, and shields other than tower shields.
Full ancestry can use Magic Stone (Sp) three times per day at caster level 3.

Each use of Magic Stone (Sp) enchants up to three touched pebbles for 30 minutes or until discharged. The printed spell lists 1d6+1 damage on a hit, or 2d6+2 against undead. Use a normal ranged attack with a +1 enhancement bonus, at a 20-ft. increment if thrown or 50 ft. if slung.
Common and Terran are automatic. Bonus languages are Celestial, Dwarven, and Ignan. Favored class Fighter.

The optional six-level Stonechild monster class starts before the full ancestry is available. Its starting adjustments are +2 Constitution, +2 Intelligence, and −2 Charisma. It starts Medium with 30-ft. speed, darkvision 60 ft., acid and poison immunity, and the listed proficiencies.

At monster-class level 1, gain 1d8 racial Hit Die, BAB +1, base saves +2, one feat, and (8 + Intelligence modifier) × 4 skill points. At level 2 add +2 Strength and +2 Constitution and reach +1 natural armor.

At level 3 add another +2 Strength and +2 Constitution. Natural armor rises to +2 and Magic Stone becomes available 1/day at caster level 3. At level 4 gain the second 1d8 racial Hit Die, BAB +2 total, base saves +3, (8 + Intelligence modifier) skill points and bonus Blind-Fight.

At level 5 add +2 Strength and +2 Constitution, reach +3 natural armor, and use Magic Stone 2/day. At level 6 add +2 Strength, reach +4 natural armor, and use Magic Stone 3/day. Its caster level stays 3.

The monster class incorporates the four points of level adjustment and ends with the same two racial Hit Dice and full traits. Complete it before multiclassing. Table 4–5 lists CR 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, and 3 for its six levels.

Full ancestry gives +2 natural armor. Cold resistance 5 applies to both mundane and magical cold damage.

Two racial Hit Dice give 2d8, BAB +2, base Fortitude +0, Reflex +3, and Will +3. One racial feat and 5 × (2 + Intelligence modifier) skill points. Racial class skills are Climb, Hide, Jump, Listen, Search, Spot, and Survival.
Racial proficiency covers simple weapons. Armor and shield proficiency come from other sources, such as class.
The full ancestry has two claws dealing 1d6 piercing and slashing damage each. In a full attack with a manufactured weapon, a free claw can be used as a secondary attack.

Powerful Build counts size as one category larger when advantageous on opposed checks with size modifiers and against size-dependent special attacks. It enables weapons one size larger and preserves actual space and reach. It stacks with size changes that preserve the trait.
Mountain Movement treats standing long jumps and high jumps as running jumps. An accelerated Climb check moves half speed as a move action without the usual −5 penalty.
Acclimated removes the Dungeon Master’s Guide p. 90 altitude penalties and persists after time at lower elevations.
Goliath Blood counts the Feral Gargun as a Goliath for effects keyed to race, including race-restricted magic items.
The language entry gives Gol-Kaa. Favored class Barbarian. Level adjustment +2 gives ECL 4 with the two racial Hit Dice before adding class levels.
The optional four-level Feral Gargun monster class starts with +2 Strength, −2 Intelligence, −2 Charisma, 30-ft. speed, darkvision 60 ft., Cold resistance 5, Goliath Blood, and Mountain Movement.
Monster-class level 1 gives 1d8, BAB +1, base Fortitude +0, Reflex +2 and Will +2, one feat, and two 1d4 claws. Level 2 adds +2 Strength, +2 Constitution, +1 natural armor, and Acclimated.

Monster-class level 3 adds the second 1d8, BAB +2 total, base Fortitude +0, Reflex +3 and Will +3, Powerful Build, and 1d6 claws. Level 4 adds +2 Constitution and +2 Dexterity and brings natural armor to +2 total.

Skill points for the progression are (2 + Intelligence modifier) × 4 at 1st level and (2 + Intelligence modifier) at 3rd. The four levels incorporate level adjustment. Complete the progression before multiclassing. Table 4–4 lists CR 1, 1, 2, and 2.

+2 racial on saving throws against sleep and charm effects.
+2 racial on Bluff, Intimidate, and Sense Motive checks.

Minor Change Shape (Su) is an at-will full-round action that physically alters the Changeling’s body, including facial features, skin color and texture, and size within the limits of disguise self. Clothing and possessions keep their appearance.

Within the disguise self limits, height can vary by up to 1 ft. and build can vary while keeping the same basic body plan. The new appearance retains the Changeling’s game traits. Wizards’ 3.5 FAQ gives the appearance of a Warforged as an example.
Minor Change Shape grants +10 circumstance on Disguise checks when used to create a disguise. The form lasts until another change. True seeing reveals the natural form, and death restores it.
In this printing, Changelings can copy a dragonmark’s appearance. Their ancestry does not develop dragonmarks or confer their powers.

traits: Medium Humanoid with a 30-ft. base land speed and no racial ability adjustments. The Expanded Psionics Handbook gives the Psionic subtype to creatures with racial psi-like abilities.
+2 racial on saving throws against mind-affecting spells and abilities and against possession.
+2 racial on Bluff, Diplomacy, and Intimidate checks. +2 racial on Disguise when impersonating a human.
Kalashtar sleep. They are immune to dream, nightmare, and other effects that rely on their ability to dream.
Naturally Psionic adds 1 extra power point per character level to the character’s reserve, even without taking a psionic class.

Racial Mindlink (Ps) 1/day is separate from the power point reserve. Resolve it as a Wilder of half the Kalashtar’s Hit Dice, rounded down, minimum manifester level 1. It grants no general manifester levels.

With the Expanded Psionics Handbook, use its Mindlink rules. At manifester level 1, use a standard action to link with one willing creature of Intelligence 3 or higher within 25 ft. for 10 minutes. The willing target gets no saving throw. Power resistance applies as harmless. Treat it as mind-affecting.

With psionics rules, initial range is 25 ft. + 5 ft. per two manifester levels, and duration is 10 minutes per manifester level. Resolve psi-like augmentation as if power points equal to its effective manifester level were spent, without deducting from the reserve. Mindlink costs 1 point before augmentation. One extra point adds a target within 15 ft. of another target. Four extra points allow a link with an unwilling target (Will negates, DC 11 + the Kalashtar’s Charisma modifier for racial Mindlink).

Without the Expanded Psionics Handbook, use the setting book’s fallback. Link with one willing creature of Intelligence 3 or higher within 30 ft. for 1 round per character level. There is no saving throw or spell resistance. The ability is mind-affecting.
Once formed, either link carries telepathic communication across any distance on the same plane without requiring a shared language. The bond conveys no influence or control.

Common and Quor are automatic. Bonus languages are Draconic and Riedran. Favored class Psion. The setting entry lists no racial Hit Dice or level adjustment. Its original setting rules give Kalashtar no dragonmarks.

Low-light vision doubles human range and preserves color and detail. +2 racial on Balance, Climb, and Jump.
Common is automatic. Bonus languages are Elven, Gnome, Halfling, and Sylvan. Favored class Ranger.

Shifting (Su) is a free action once per day. It lasts 3 rounds + the current Constitution modifier, counting an increase from shifting. Each shifter feat adds one round per use, and each pair of shifter feats adds one daily use.
Choose one of the six original traits at character creation. Its active benefits apply while shifting. Shifting is innate and cannot be transmitted by bites or claws.
Beasthide gives +2 Constitution and a +2 natural armor bonus to AC.
Cliffwalk gives +2 Dexterity and a climb speed of 20 ft.
Longstride gives +2 Dexterity and +10 ft. to base land speed.

Longtooth gives +2 Strength and a bite with a printed base die of 1d6 and +1 damage per four character levels. Bite once per round. When paired with a weapon, the bite is a secondary natural attack with −5 on the bite attack roll and half the Strength bonus to damage.

Razorclaw gives +2 Strength and two primary claws with printed base damage 1d4 +1 per four character levels per claw. Use one claw as a standard action or both as a full attack. Each claw attacks at most once per round. In the first printing, using a claw as a light off-hand weapon with a manufactured primary weapon applies −2 to all attacks that round.
Wildhunt gives +2 Constitution and scent while shifting. Outside shifting, Wildhunt gives +2 to Survival checks.

Wildhunt scent detects a creature at 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind, or 15 ft. downwind. Double those ranges for strong odors and triple them for overpowering odors. A move action identifies direction. Within 5 ft., pinpoint the source.

While shifting, a Wildhunt Shifter with Track can follow scent using Survival. A typical fresh trail is DC 10 and adds +2 per hour, with adjustments for odor and group size. Ignore surface and poor-visibility modifiers.

species.name: Spellscale
traits: Medium Humanoid with the Dragonblood subtype. +2 Charisma, −2 Constitution. Base land speed 30 ft. Low-light vision preserves color and detail in dim light at twice human range.

A Spellscale counts as a dragon for racial effects. The subtype also affects eligibility for dragon-specific abilities, feats, and items, and makes the Spellscale subject to harmful dragon-targeted effects. The creature type remains Humanoid.
Common and Draconic are automatic. Bonus languages are Dwarven, Elven, Gnome, and Halfling. Favored class Sorcerer. No racial Hit Dice or level adjustment are added.

Blood Quickening takes one hour and grants the benefits of one chosen dragon deity for 24 hours. Choose at most one meditation per day. A check bonus is racial and equals half character level, rounded down. Borrowed feats cannot meet prerequisites and still use the normal feat rules.

Aasterinian grants a Disguise bonus and three uses of Improved Counterspell. Astilabor grants an Appraise bonus and Eschew Materials all day. Chronepsis grants a Listen bonus and Silent Spell for the day.
Bahamut adds 2d6 damage to one evil creature targeted by or in the area of the spell, up to three times. Tiamat works the same way against a good creature.
Falazure treats inflict spells as on your spell list for spell completion and spell trigger items. Tamara does the same for cure spells. These meditations allow item use and grant no spells known.

Garyx grants two uses of Widen Spell. Hlal provides a Perform (storytelling) bonus and three uses of Heighten Spell. Io gives a Spellcraft bonus and three uses of Empower Spell. Lendys gives a Concentration bonus and Still Spell for the day.

The optional Rite of Spellscale Assumption converts a willing nondraconic Humanoid. Over seven consecutive days the officiating Spellscale must be able to cast polymorph and have 10 ranks in Knowledge (arcana). Materials cost 2,000 gp. The rite replaces racial traits and removes former racial Hit Dice and level adjustment. Existing languages and favored classes are retained, with Draconic and Sorcerer added.

species.name: Dragonborn of Bahamut
traits: For the Rite of Rebirth, Bahamut calls a willing, non-evil subject of Intelligence 3 or higher. The rite takes 24 hours of fasting and meditation followed by 24 hours of sleep in a symbolic egg. The egg costs 100 gp and requires metallic dragon scales. An interruption restarts the rite.

Retain original type, subtypes, racial Hit Dice, racial ability adjustments, size, powerful build if present, base speed and other movement modes, languages already known, favored classes, and level adjustment. Add Dragonblood under the subtype rules, +2 Constitution, −2 Dexterity, Draconic, and favored class Fighter. Continue to count as the original race and as a dragon for race-related effects.

Other former racial traits go away, including racial bonus feats, extra racial skill points, and special movement perks such as a dwarf’s full armored speed. Remove lost bonus points from ranks. Recheck feat and prestige-class prerequisites. The rite permits one eligible feat swap for a first-level-only Dragonblood feat. Dragonborn Paladins may multiclass and later resume Paladin.

The dragonborn emerges as an adult and loses former age adjustments. The new middle, old, and venerable ages are 200, 300, and 400 years. Add 2d% to 400 years for maximum age. Gain +2 dodge AC against creatures of the Dragon type and immunity to dragons’ frightful presence. Choose one permanent aspect: Heart, Mind, or Wings.

Heart grants a line 5 ft. per Hit Die (maximum 100 ft.), usable once every 1d4 rounds. Damage is 1d8 plus 1d8 per three Hit Dice. Choose acid, cold, electricity, or fire each time. Reflex DC 10 + half Hit Dice, rounded down, + Constitution modifier halves damage.

Mind grants immunity to paralysis and magic sleep, low-light vision, darkvision 30 ft., and +2 racial to Listen, Search, and Spot. Darkvision reaches 60 ft. at 6 HD, 90 ft. at 9 HD, and 120 ft. at 12 HD. Low-light range rises to three times human at 9 HD and four times at 12 HD. Blindsense 30 ft. starts at 15 HD.

Wings grants +10 racial to Jump and gliding at 30 ft. with average maneuverability. Glide 20 ft. forward per 5 ft. descended and take no falling damage while gliding. No hovering or gliding with a medium or heavy load. If helpless or unconscious in midair, the wings cause a slow descent and reduce falling damage to 1d6.

Wings flight starts at 6 HD, 30 ft. with average maneuverability. Flight requires a light load and no fatigue or exhaustion. Fly safely for Constitution modifier rounds in a row (minimum 1). Extend a flight up to twice that safe duration and become fatigued at the end. More than 10 minutes of powered flight in a day also causes fatigue. Gliding can separate powered flights. Powered flight stops causing that fatigue at 12 HD.

While flying, a dive attack functions as a charge with at least 30 ft. of travel and 10 ft. of descent. The dive requires a piercing weapon and deals double damage on a hit. Running in flight requires a straight line.

species.name: Warforged
traits: Medium Construct with the Living Construct subtype and a Constitution score. Base land speed 30 ft. +2 Constitution, −2 Wisdom, and −2 Charisma. Class determines Hit Dice, BAB, saves, and skill points. The playable entry lists no level adjustment.

Use ordinary vision and normal saves against mind-affecting spells and abilities. Living Constructs are subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, stunning, ability damage and drain, death effects, and necromancy.
Immune to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, disease, nausea, fatigue, exhaustion, effects causing sickened, and energy drain.

The official errata allows natural recovery of nonlethal damage and bars natural healing of lethal damage. Healing-subschool spells and supernatural healing of HP or ability damage work at half effect. Repair light damage works at full effect.
Effects that target living creatures or constructs can affect a Warforged. Raise dead and resurrection can restore one to life.

The p. 46 Craft repair procedure takes 8 hours and restores 1 HP per point the check exceeds 15. The procedure requires ranks, as clarified in the errata. Use Craft (armorsmithing, blacksmithing, gemcutting, or sculpting), including for self-repair. Taking 10 is allowed. Taking 20 is barred.

Heat metal, chill metal, and repel metal or stone affect Warforged as if they wore metal armor. Repel wood also applies. Rusting grasp deals 2d6 damage, Reflex half at DC 14 + caster ability modifier. A rust monster’s touch deals 2d6, Reflex DC 17 half.

At 0 HP, a Warforged is disabled and gets one move or standard action per round without losing HP for strenuous actions. At −1 through −9 HP it is inert, unconscious and helpless, and loses HP only if damaged again.
Warforged function without food, sleep, or air. A Warforged can benefit from consumables. Spell preparation and infusions retain their class rest requirements.

Composite Plating gives a +2 armor bonus to AC. It occupies the armor and magic robe slot and can be enchanted as armor. The plating prevents wearing other armor or magic robes and does not stack with other armor bonuses. It imposes 5% arcane spell failure unless a class feature waives failure in light armor.
Light Fortification gives a 25% chance to negate the extra effects of a critical hit or sneak attack and roll damage normally.
One natural slam deals 1d4 base damage. Common is automatic, with no racial bonus languages. Favored class Fighter.

Adamantine Body is an optional 1st-level feat. It sets the plating armor bonus to +8, grants DR 2/adamantine, reduces base speed to 20 ft., and counts as heavy armor. Maximum Dexterity bonus +1, armor check penalty −5, and arcane spell failure 35%.

species.name: Rilkan
traits: Medium Humanoid with the Reptilian subtype. +2 Dexterity, −2 Strength. Base land speed 30 ft. The racial traits grant no essentia pool. Gaining an essentia pool from a class or feat adds the Incarnum subtype.
Racial Knowledge treats all Knowledge checks as trained, even without ranks. Its +1 competence bonus on Knowledge and bardic knowledge checks increases by +1 per two soulmelds currently shaped.
+2 racial bonus to Bluff and Diplomacy.
Racial Aid gives +3 to the roll of another Rilkan when you successfully aid them. Use the ordinary bonus when aiding a creature of another species.
Common is automatic. Bonus languages can be any nonsecret language. Favored class Incarnate. The published examples list LA +0 and use class Hit Dice.
Rilkans resemble humans with bands of pebbly scales on the neck and forearms. The book describes single-color bands in males and patterned multicolor bands in females.
Choose the optional Rilkan Rogue substitutions at Rogue 1, 3, and 10 independently. Each uses a d6 Hit Die and adds Speak Language as a class skill at that level.
Rogue 1 keeps trapfinding and trades 1st-level sneak attack for Improved Flanking. Sneak attack begins at Rogue 3 and stays 1d6 below the standard progression if this substitution is taken.
Improved Flanking gives the Rilkan Rogue +4 to attacks when flanking in place of the usual +2. Other Rilkans flanking that same foe also get +4. Allies of other species use the usual flanking bonus.

The Rogue 3 substitution grants bardic knowledge and a bonus feat. It replaces trap sense and prevents gaining it from later rogue levels. Use rogue level plus Intelligence modifier for bardic knowledge, and apply Racial Knowledge. The feat choices are Deceitful, Diligent, Investigator, Negotiator, and Persuasive.

Rogue 10 can replace that level’s special ability with Fortunate Reflexes. Reroll a failed Reflex save unless the original die was a natural 1, and keep the new result. Taking this option gives up improved evasion from rogue levels.

species.name: Azurin
traits: Medium Humanoid with the Human and Incarnum subtypes. No racial ability score adjustments. Base land speed 30 ft. The Human subtype makes Azurins count as human for applicable effects. The Incarnum subtype supplies no shared abilities or defenses.
Gain one bonus feat at 1st level. Azurin traits do not grant the human bonus skill points.

The racial essentia pool increases permanently by 1. This creates a pool of 1 if the character has no other source. An essentia pool supplies points to invest in eligible feats, soulmelds, and abilities.

Normal capacity per investment is 1 at levels 1–5, 2 at 6–11, 3 at 12–17, and 4 at 18–20. Soulmeld investments can be reallocated as a swift action. Incarnum feat investments are normally set once per day and locked for 24 hours.
Common is automatic. Bonus languages can be any nonsecret language. Favored class Soulborn. The published examples list LA +0 and use class Hit Dice.
Azurins resemble their human families. A sky-blue sheen in the whites of the eyes is their distinguishing physical trait.

species.name: Duskling
traits: Medium Fey with the Incarnum subtype. +2 Constitution, −2 Intelligence. Base land speed 30 ft. Low-light vision doubles human range with color and detail.

Effects that specifically target humanoids, such as charm person, cannot target a Duskling. The species chooses a fixed home plane at character creation with DM approval. On the Material Plane it has the Extraplanar subtype.
The Incarnum subtype marks eligibility for targeted effects. The permanent racial essentia pool increases by 1, or starts at 1 if the character has no other source.
Racial movement gives a +5-ft. enhancement bonus to land speed per invested essentia. It applies with light or no armor and a light load.
Reallocate essentia among the eligible investments as a swift action on your turn. Pool size and the capacity of each investment are separate.
Normal capacity per investment is 1 at character levels 1–5, 2 at 6–11, 3 at 12–17, and 4 at 18–20.

Common and Sylvan are automatic. Bonus languages are Elf (the book’s name for Elven), Gnoll, Gnome, Goblin, and Halfling. Favored class Totemist. The published examples list LA +0 and use class Hit Dice.

The optional 1st-level Duskling Barbarian substitution uses a d10 Hit Die. Incarnum Speed replaces Fast Movement. Each invested point gives a +10-ft. enhancement bonus to base land speed with up to medium armor and a medium load. Each point also gives +2 insight on initiative checks, regardless of armor or load. The two enhancement bonuses to speed do not stack.

The optional d10 Barbarian substitutions at 7th and 11th level grant Incarnum Defense and Incarnum Rage respectively. Defense replaces Barbarian damage reduction and gives DR 1/— plus resistance 1 to each energy type per point. Incarnum Rage replaces Greater Rage and grants 2 essentia during rage. Greater Rage then replaces Mighty Rage if reached.

species.name: Tibbit
traits: Small Monstrous Humanoid with the Shapechanger subtype, as corrected by Paizo’s errata. +2 Dexterity, −2 Strength, 20-ft. land speed, darkvision 60 ft., and +2 racial to Spot, Jump, and Escape Artist.

Small size gives +1 AC and attack, +4 Hide, Small weapon sizes, and three quarters of Medium carrying capacity. Humanoid-only spells such as charm person do not affect Tibbits. Class levels supply their Hit Dice, with no added level adjustment.

Feline Transformation lets a Tibbit become a house cat at will as a standard action. The rules give no duration limit. Returning to humanoid form takes a full-round action. Wait one hour after returning before transforming again.

Cat form is Tiny and has 30-ft. land speed, +2 size AC and attack, +8 size Hide, −8 Strength to a minimum of 3, and +2 Dexterity on top of humanoid-form scores. It gains scent and keeps its creature type and otherwise unchanged abilities.
Cat form gains two primary claws (1d2 base damage) and a secondary bite (1d3 base damage). A full attack uses both claws and the bite at −5. Base attack bonus gives no additional natural attacks.

Equipment generally melds into the cat. Armor, shields, weapons, and robes stop providing benefits. Items with a suitable worn shape may continue giving passive benefits when they reshape into something a cat can wear.
Cat form cannot speak, manipulate fine objects, cast spells with verbal or somatic components, use scrolls, or activate magic items.
Death in cat form causes reversion after one round. Effects that see through polymorph reveal the Tibbit. Magic aura detection alone does not reveal the disguise.

Common and Feline are automatic, with any bonus language and Rogue as the favored class. Feline is shared with cats of Intelligence 3 or higher, permitting Diplomacy with them. Other races cannot learn it or bridge it with tongues.

species.name: Skarn
traits: Medium Humanoid with the Reptilian subtype. +2 Strength, −2 Dexterity. Base land speed 30 ft. The racial traits grant no essentia pool. Gaining a pool from a class or feat adds the Incarnum subtype.

Natural Weapon: One arm-spine attack per round under the base racial rule. It deals 1d6 piercing. An off-hand spine attack takes the ordinary off-hand penalties and adds only half a positive Strength modifier to damage.
An arm cannot attack with both its spines and a weapon it wields in the same round. Attacking with spines on an arm carrying a shield removes that shield’s AC bonus until the start of your next turn.
Binding a soulmeld to the arms chakra makes spine attacks count as lawful for overcoming damage reduction.

+2 racial bonus to Intimidate and Climb. Common is automatic. Bonus languages are Draconic, Elf (Elven), Celestial, Abyssal, and Infernal. Favored class Incarnate. The published examples list LA +0 and use class Hit Dice.
Skarn are solidly built and humanlike, with rows of spines on their forearms, calves, and upper back. The spines can lie flush against the body and do not retract.
Choose the optional Skarn Monk substitutions at Monk 1, 5, and 10 independently. Each uses a d8 Hit Die and adds Intimidate as a class skill at that level.

Monk 1 replaces the unarmed strike class feature with Spine Strike. Treat arm spines as unarmed strikes for Monk class features such as flurry of blows and ki strike. Medium Monk damage with spines rises to 1d8 at Monk 4 and 1d10 at Monk 8.

Monk 5 grants one essentia and Defensive Insight, replacing the standard level-based Monk AC bonus. Gain +1 insight AC per invested point. It applies to touch AC and while flat-footed, immobilized, or helpless, and works with armor, shield, or heavy load. The normal Wisdom-to-AC rules still apply separately.

Monk 10 replaces ki strike (lawful) with one daily soulmeld from the Soulborn list if Constitution is at least 11, plus the ability to bind a soulmeld to the arms chakra. Meldshaper level is half Monk level. Save DC is 10 + invested essentia + Wisdom modifier.

traits: Medium Monstrous Humanoid. +2 Constitution, −2 Dexterity, −2 Intelligence. Base land speed 30 ft. Darkvision 60 ft. Carapace gives +4 natural armor. Humanoid-only effects such as charm person and hold person do not affect Diopsids.
Bioluminescence can be lit or doused at will as a free action. It sheds light in a 10-ft. radius and shadowy illumination for 20 ft. beyond that.
Wings can be unfurled as an immediate action to descend at 60 ft. per round without falling damage. They grant no flight. A paralyzed, unconscious, or otherwise incapacitated Diopsid cannot use them.

Two strong primary arms and two weaker supporting arms. With the lower arms available for support, wield a weapon up to one size category larger without the normal size penalty. A Large longsword can be held by one primary arm and steadied by its matching lower arm.

Using all four hands, wield two two-handed weapons as a pair. Each gets full two-handed damage, including 1½ times a positive Strength modifier. Use the ordinary two-weapon attack penalties for a non-light off-hand weapon.

When a primary hand carries an item, an extra weapon used in a lower arm adds only half a positive Strength modifier. Each extra light weapon imposes −4 on all attacks, or −8 if the extra weapon is one-handed. The lower arms alone cannot wield a two-handed weapon. A lower-arm shield applies its armor check penalty to attacks and skill checks even if proficient.
Limb Symmetry waives the Dexterity prerequisite for feats with “two-weapon” in their name. Other prerequisites still apply. One free hand is enough for somatic components.

Light armor has no additional racial penalty. Medium armor imposes −2 Dexterity and heavy armor imposes −4 Dexterity. All armor must be custom-made and priced as one size larger. Diopsids do not need sleep and are immune to sleep effects.

Common and Diopsid are automatic. Bonus languages are Dwarf (Dwarven), Orc, Terran, and Undercommon. The native language uses light signals, including darkvision-only flashes. Spot detects the exchange in place of Listen. Those without bioluminescence can learn to understand and translate it.
Favored class Barbarian. LA +1. The playable profile adds no racial Hit Dice.
